The petitioners have filed this petition seeking following reliefs:-
"10. (a) Call for the entire records pertaining to the present case.

b) Issue a Writ of Mandamus directing the Respondent Authorities to initiate the Land Acquisition proceedings for the acquisition of the lands belonging to the Petitioners herein which already stands utilised by the Municipal Corporation,
Raipur, in accordance with the prevailing applicable law, in a time bound manner.

c) Issue a Writ of Mandamus directing the Respondent Authorities to conclude the said Acquisition Proceedings by calculating the Compensation payable to the Petitioners herein as per the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2020) 2 SCC 569: Vidya Devi v. State of Himachal Pradesh & others as well as the Judgements rendered by the Hon'ble High Court of Chhattisgarh in Writ Appeal no. 241/2020:
Ramkrishna Sahu v. State of Chhattisgarh on 09.02.2023 & in Writ Appeal no.
51/2019: M/s.
Natural Collections (LLP), Raipur v. State of Chhattisgarh on 09.03.2023.
d) Issue a Writ of Mandamus directing the Respondent Authorities to conclude the said Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19287 -3- Acquisition Proceedings by depositing of the Award Amount as contemplated under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation & Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 along with Interest @ 12% per annum till the amount is paid.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are the owner of the land bearing kh. no.193/1 and 193/2 measuring 0.462 hectares.
They became owner of the land pursuant to registered sale deed executed in their favour on 12.01.1999.

Respondent /Municipal Corporation Raipur have constructed road and also drain over the portion of private ownership land of the petitioners without acquiring the same in accordance with law and making payment of suitable amount of compensation.
Petitioners thereafter have approached the authority, however, no heed was given on their request.
Petitioners thereafter had got his land demarcated by filing Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19287 -4- application under Section 129 of the Land Revenue Code.
As per demarcation report, revenue officials have found that the road and drain is constructed on portion of private ownership land of the petitioners.
Demarcation report to this effect is filed as Annexure P-5.

Petitioners thereafter submitted representation before respondent No.4 along with copy of the demarcation report making request to initiate land acquisition proceeding of the land on which road and drain is constructed and to make payment of compensation, however, the representation submitted by the petitioner till date has not been decided or replied to the petitioners.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the respondent- Municipal Corporation be directed to take decision on the pending representation.

3. Learned counsel for respondents No. 3 & 4/ Municipal Corporation submits that the detail facts have not been pleaded in the writ petition as to on which portion of land drain and road was constructed.
The document which is stated to be representation is in fact a notice under Section 401 of the Municipal Corporation Act.
If petitioners submit fresh representation the claim of the petitioners can be considered in accordance with law.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the documents annexed along with this petition.

5. Taking into consideration the nature of grievance raised in the writ petition in particular the grievance of the petitioners based on demarcation report that respondents No. 3 & 4 have Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19287 -5- constructed drain and road over the portion of ownership land of the petitioners, without commenting anything on merits of claim of the petitioners, this writ petition is disposed of permitting the petitioners to file fresh representation before respondents No. 3 & 4 raising all the grievances along with supporting documents and in the event the petitioners file fresh representation, respondents No. 3 & 4 shall consider and decide the same in accordance with law,
expeditiously, preferably within a period of 3 months from the date of receipt of representation.
Sd/---/-/-/-/--------/--/-
(Parth Prateem Sahu) Judge Praveen Smt. Kavita Bisen vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84069269/
